chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Sama'a from Al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfah ibn Mansur from Ubayd ibn Zurarah from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about breastfeeding, and he said: 'Breastfeeding does not make prohibited (for marriage) except what was suckled from one breast over two complete years.'

Therefore, we interpret this report as meaning that his phrase 'two complete years' is a condition/time-frame for the breastfeeding, as if he said: 'Breastfeeding does not make prohibited except what was suckled from one breast within two complete years.'
And we said this because if breastfeeding occurs after the two years, it does not make prohibited; that which indicates this is what has been narrated:

key_terms.ثَدْيٍ وَاحِدٍ: One breast (specifying the source of milk)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for breastfeeding to create a permanent marriage prohibition in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the duration requirement for breastfeeding to establish kinship prohibitions, specifying that suckling must occur within two complete years from a single breast. The scholar interprets 'two complete years' as a temporal condition for the act itself, implying that suckling after this period does not contribute to the prohibition. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining mahram relationships and marriage eligibility.
